subject: chemistry

hotspots.label: A period (row)
hotspots.description: This glowing horizontal row is one period. Its elements sit side by side and all share the same number of electron shells.
hotspots.positionHint: The highlighted horizontal row of tiles through the middle of the table section.
hotspots.function: Shows a horizontal row — one period of the periodic table.

hotspots.label: Shared shell count
hotspots.description: Every element in the row shows the same number of shells — the period number. This is the trait the whole row shares.
hotspots.positionHint: The small shell icons floating beside each row tile, visible when the shell-count layer is on.
hotspots.function: Shows the identical shell count shared across the row.

hotspots.label: Metal → nonmetal sweep
hotspots.description: Across the row the tiles shift from warm metal tones on the left to cool nonmetal tones on the right — the row is a journey across element character.
hotspots.positionHint: The gradient of tile colors along the row, visible when the character-sweep layer is on.
hotspots.function: Shows the shift from metals to nonmetals across the period.

visualStyleNotes: Chemistry palette, Anatomy Atelier bar: warm off-white/paper background (#F7F3EC) with a soft radial vignette, no floor grid, no props. A section of periodic table floats centered with one row highlighted, lit with soft neutral studio light — no rim-light glow, no bloom, no emissive anywhere. Clean stylized product-render look, specimen-quality not cartoon. Color on the mesh is restrained: table tiles are warm paper-white with faint graphite borders; the character-sweep layer tints the row tiles with a gentle warm-to-cool gradient at low saturation. Strong saturated color is reserved entirely for the small flat hotspot dots (slate / amber / coral / molecular green accents from the Chemistry palette). Slow auto-rotation, calm, minimal chrome.
materialNotes: Metallic-roughness PBR, metallic=0 everywhere, single 2K shared texture atlas. Table tiles: warm paper-white rounded squares, roughness ~0.55, subtle bevel. Shell icons: small translucent hairline rings with tiny teal electron dots. No emissive channels anywhere — any glow or highlight is handled by app runtime UI, not baked into the asset. Tile text is rendered by the app UI layer.
assetBrief:
SUBJECT: a slice of the periodic table with one row emphasized, built to be read as 'the same row = the same number of shells = a journey from metal to nonmetal.' Three procedural layers, all clean primitives:

1) MAIN: a grid of thin rounded-square tiles (paper-white, faint graphite border), 4 rows x 8 columns. The 2nd row from the top has 8 tiles given a faint muted blue-grey cast and a slightly raised bevel — this is the highlighted period. No text on the mesh (symbols render as app UI).

2) SHELL COUNT (toggleable layer): floating beside each tile of the highlighted row, a small shell icon (translucent hairline ring) — every icon shows the SAME number of tiny teal electron dots (e.g. 3) to make the shared trait visible.

3) CHARACTER SWEEP (toggleable layer): the highlighted row's tiles get a gentle low-saturation gradient — warm desaturated coral at the left, passing through soft olive, ending cool desaturated blue at the right — suggesting metals to nonmetals.

Camera: framed so the grid fills the view with the highlighted row centered; auto-rotate default. Budget 8-12k triangles. Named nodes: TableGrid, Tile_01-32, HighlightRow, ShellIcon_01-08, SweepTint. All labels are hotspot dots in the app layer; no text on the mesh.
